sentences.text: ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. L.D. Khatri For Respondent(s) : Mr. Hanuman Prajapati,
PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 06/01/2026 1.

The instant criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed on behalf of the petitioner seeking quashing of FIR No. 402/2014 registered at ACB CPS, Jaipur for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC, read with Sections 13(1)(d) and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

2. After hearing the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor, this Court,
keeping in view the fact that the investigation against the petitioner has been pending since the year 2014, and without entering into the niceties and merits of the case, deems it just and proper to direct the learned trial Court to consider and decide all the objections raised by the petitioner in the present petition at the stage of framing of charges, after filing of the charge-sheet against the petitioner, which, as submitted by the learned Public Prosecutor, is likely to be filed shortly.
(Uploaded on 07/01/2026 at 10:26:40 AM) [2026:RJ-JD:186] (2 of 2) [CRLMP-7542/2025]
3.

In view of the above, it is ordered that during the course of investigation, or till filing of the Ashok Kumar vs State Of Rajasthan (2026:Rj-Jd:186) on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31985347/
1 charge-sheet, the petitioner shall not be arrested.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Instead, he shall be informed about the filing of the charge-sheet and shall be required to appear before the concerned Court on the fixed date.
Upon filing of the charge- sheet, the petitioner shall appear before the trial Court and move a regular bail application.

In the event such bail application is filed, the learned trial Judge shall release the petitioner on bail on the very same day, keeping in view the curtailment of the petitioner's fundamental right to speedy investigation, as enunciated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Vakil Prasad Singh vs. State of Bihar, reported in AIR 2009 (3) SCC 355.
4. With the aforesaid directions, the present criminal misc. petition as well as stay petition stands disposed of.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 34-divya/-
